hindi: अब इसके बाद हम ऋतुचर्या नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on seasonal conduct (ṛtucaryā).

hindi: काल ही भगवान है, जिसका न आदि है और न अंत, जो संचित कर्मों के अनुसार चलता है। उसके अनुरोध से सूर्य आदि और आकाश आदि विशेष महाभूत जैसे-जैसे रूपांतरित होते हैं, वैसे-वैसे वे जीवधारियों के जन्म और मृत्यु के, तथा ऋतु, रस, वीर्य, दोष, देह और बल की हानियों और संपत्तियों के कारण और आधार बन जाते हैं।
english: Time, indeed, is the Lord, without beginning or end, who follows the actions as they have accumulated. In compliance with him the sun and the rest, and space and the rest, the particular great elements (mahābhūta), change in one way and another, and so become the cause and the ground of the birth and death of living beings, and of the failings and successes of the seasons, tastes (rasa), potency (vīrya), doṣas, body and strength.

text_flags.why: space misplaced: printed "khādaya śca" is khādayaś ca (khādayaḥ + ca, sandhi ḥ+c > ś); no letter is missing

notes: Printed "khādaya śca" is read as khādayaḥ + ca. "yathopacitakarmānusārī": the actions are those accumulated (by beings) is the natural sense; the text does not name whose. "kālo hi nāma" = "Time, so called, indeed". "janma-maraṇasya" is singular while "janmavatām" is plural, as printed. "vyāpat-saṃpad" read as failure/ruin and success/perfection.
lines_deva: कालो हि नाम भगवाननादि निधनो यथोपचितकर्मानुसारी यदनुरोधादादित्यादयः खादय श्च महाभूतविशेषास्तथातथा विपरिणमंतो जन्मवतां जन्ममरणस्यर्तुरसवीर्यदोषदेहबलव्यापत्संपदां च कारणत्वं प्रत्ययतां प्रतिपद्यंते ॥
lines_iast: kālo hi nāma bhagavānanādi nidhano yathopacitakarmānusārī yadanurodhādādityādayaḥ khādaya śca mahābhūtaviśeṣāstathātathā vipariṇamaṃto janmavatāṃ janmamaraṇasyarturasavīryadoṣadehabalavyāpatsaṃpadāṃ ca kāraṇatvaṃ pratyayatāṃ pratipadyaṃte ||

words.gloss: by the division into mātrā, kāṣṭhā ... year

hindi: वह काल मात्रा, काष्ठा, कला, नाडिका, मुहूर्त, याम, अहोरात्र, पक्ष, मास, ऋतु, अयन और वर्ष के भेद से बारह प्रकार से विभाजित किया जाता है।
english: That (Time) is divided twelvefold, by the divisions mātrā, kāṣṭhā, kalā, nāḍikā, muhūrta, yāma, day-and-night (ahorātra), fortnight (pakṣa), month (māsa), season (ṛtu), half-year course (ayana) and year (varṣa).

hindi: उनमें आँख का झपकना एक मात्रा है।
english: Among these, the twinkling of the eye is a mātrā.

hindi: वे पंद्रह मात्राएँ एक काष्ठा हैं।
english: Those (mātrās), fifteen, make a kāṣṭhā.
notes: "tāḥ" is feminine plural and takes its antecedent (mātrās) from the preceding unit.

hindi: वे तीस काष्ठाएँ एक कला हैं।
english: Those (kāṣṭhās), thirty, make a kalā.
notes: The text has only "tāḥ triṃśat kalā"; the antecedent of "tāḥ" (kāṣṭhās) comes from the preceding unit.

hindi: वे बीस कलाएँ, दसवें भाग सहित, एक नाडिका हैं।
english: Those (kalās), twenty together with a tenth part, make a nāḍikā.
notes: "sadaśabhāgā" read as sa-daśa-bhāgā, "having a tenth part (added)". The text does not say a tenth of what; the antecedent of "tāḥ" (kalās) comes from the preceding unit. Literal rendering only.

hindi: दो नाडिकाएँ भी एक मुहूर्त हैं।
english: A pair of nāḍikās is also a muhūrta.
notes: "ca" is rendered "also"; it may simply link this unit to the series.

words.gloss: when night and day are equal
words.gram: bahuvrīhi, loc. sg. (qualifying rāśi-bhāge, or absolute)

words.gloss: in the division of the total

hindi: वे, जब दिन और रात बराबर हों, राशि के भाग में, चौथाई कम चार मिलकर एक याम होते हैं।
english: Those (muhūrtas), when day and night are equal, in the division of the total (rāśi), four less a quarter make a yāma.
notes: Marked "verse" but reads as prose. "te" is taken as muhūrtas (masculine plural, from unit 8). "rāśi-bhāge" is obscure: rāśi = heap/total; I read "in the division of the total", the exact sense is uncertain. "tulya-rātriṃdive" read as a locative of day and night being equal.
lines_deva: ते तुल्यरात्रिंदिवे राशिभागे चत्वारः पादोना यामः ॥
lines_iast: te tulyarātriṃdive rāśibhāge catvāraḥ pādonā yāmaḥ ||

hindi: उन चारों से दिन होता है और रात भी।
english: By those four there is the day, and the night.
notes: "taiḥ caturbhiḥ" refers to the yāmas of the preceding unit (masculine plural); the text is brief and does not say "each".

hindi: पंद्रह अहोरात्र एक पक्ष हैं।
english: Fifteen day-and-night periods make a fortnight (pakṣa).

hindi: दो पक्ष एक मास हैं।
english: A pair of fortnights is a month (māsa).

hindi: वह मास शुक्ल पर समाप्त होने वाला है।
english: That month ends with the bright (śukla) fortnight.
notes: "sa" refers to māsa of the preceding unit; "śukla" is read as the bright fortnight.

hindi: मार्गशीर्ष से आरंभ होने वाले उन मासों से दो-दो की संख्या में क्रम से हेमंत, शिशिर, वसंत, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा और शरद नाम की छह ऋतुएँ होती हैं।
english: By those (months) beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa, taken two by two in order, there come to be six seasons (ṛtu) named Hemanta, Śiśira, Vasanta, Grīṣma, Varṣā and Śarad.

text_flags.why: possible: taiḥ + mār- gives "tair mār-"; the r is missing in the scan

notes: The compound hemanta-śiśira-vasanta-grīṣma-varṣā-śarad-ākhyāḥ is split by the printed space after "hemantaśiśira".

hindi: उनमें शिशिर आदि तीन ऋतुएँ सूर्य का उत्तरायण और आदान हैं, और शेष तीन दक्षिणायन और विसर्ग हैं।
english: Among them, the three beginning with Śiśira are the sun's northward course (udagayana) and ādāna (taking-in); the remaining three are the southward course (dakṣiṇāyana) and visarga (release).
notes: "raveḥ" (of the sun) is read with both courses. "ādāna" and "visarga" are kept as terms, glossed literally as taking-in and release.
lines_deva: तेषु शिशिरादयस्त्रयो रवेरुदगयनमादानं च शेषा दक्षिणायनं विसर्गश्च ॥
lines_iast: teṣu śiśirādayastrayo raverudagayanamādānaṃ ca śeṣā dakṣiṇāyanaṃ visargaśca ||

hindi: आदान और विसर्ग वे दोनों मिलकर एक वर्ष हैं।
english: Those two, ādāna and visarga, make a year (varṣa).

text_flags.why: possible: final m lost in the scan (neuter nominative singular varṣam)

hindi: उन दोनों में आदान आग्नेय है।
english: Of those two, ādāna is fiery (āgneya).

words.gloss: taken up by time's nature and course
whose disc has a net of very hot rays

hindi: उस आदान काल में काल के स्वभाव और मार्ग से अधिकृत सूर्य, जिसका मंडल अत्यंत उष्ण किरणों के जाल वाला है, तथा उसके संपर्क से तीव्र और रूखी वायुएँ, सोम से उत्पन्न गुण को सुखाते हुए, संसार की स्निग्धता को लेते हुए, और ऋतुओं के क्रम से उत्पन्न रूखेपन के कारण रूखे रसों, अर्थात तिक्त, कषाय और कटु को अत्यंत प्रबल करते हुए, मनुष्यों में दुर्बलता लाते हैं।
english: In that (ādāna), indeed, the sun, taken up by the nature and course of time, its disc a net of exceedingly hot rays, and, through contact with it, the winds, sharp and dry, drying up the quality born of Soma (the moon), taking away the moisture of the world, and, through the dryness produced by the sequence of the seasons, greatly strengthening the dry tastes (rasa), bitter, astringent and pungent, bring weakness to men.
notes: One sentence with two subjects (the sun and the winds) and plural participles. "kāla-svabhāva-mārga-parigṛhītaḥ" is ambiguous (seized/governed by the nature and course of time); a literal rendering is given. "soma-jam guṇam" = the quality born of Soma, i.e. the moon, as the text says. "tasmin" refers to ādāna of unit 17.
lines_deva: तस्मिन् खलु कालस्वभावमार्गपरिगृहीतोऽत्यर्थोष्णगभस्तिजालमंडलोऽर्कस्तत्संपर्काद्वायवश्च तीव्ररूक्षाः सोमजं गुणमुपशोषयंतो जगतः स्नेहमाददाना ऋतुक्रमेणोपजनितरौक्ष्याद्रूक्षान् रसांस्तिक्तकषायकटुकानभिप्रबलयंतो नृणां दौर्बल्यमावहंति ॥
lines_iast: tasmin khalu kālasvabhāvamārgaparigṛhīto'tyarthoṣṇagabhastijālamaṃḍalo'rkastatsaṃparkādvāyavaśca tīvrarūkṣāḥ somajaṃ guṇamupaśoṣayaṃto jagataḥ snehamādadānā ṛtukrameṇopajanitaraukṣyādrūkṣān rasāṃstiktakaṣāyakaṭukānabhiprabalayaṃto nṛṇāṃ daurbalyamāvahaṃti ||

hindi: विसर्ग तो सौम्य है।
english: Visarga, however, is saumya (gentle, of the nature of Soma, the moon).

words.gloss: whose power is struck down by time's course, cloud, wind, rain

words.gram: pres. pass. part. ā-√pyāy, n. loc. sg.

words.gloss: whose heat is quieted by Mahendra's water

hindi: उस विसर्ग में भी, जब काल के मार्ग, मेघ, वायु और वर्षा से सूर्य का प्रभाव दब गया हो और सूर्य दक्षिणायन में हो, चंद्रमा का बल अबाधित हो, संसार चंद्रमा की शीतल किरणों से निरंतर तृप्त हो रहा हो और महेंद्र के जल से उसका ताप शांत हो गया हो, तब अरूखे रस, अर्थात अम्ल, लवण और मधुर, क्रम से बढ़ते हैं और मनुष्यों का बल संचित होता है, ऐसा।
english: In that (visarga) also, when the sun, going in the southern course, has its power struck down by the course of time, clouds, wind and rain, and the moon is of unimpeded strength, and the world is constantly refreshed by cool rays and its heat is quieted by the water of Mahendra (Indra), the non-dry tastes, sour, salty and sweet, increase in due order, and the strength of men is built up. Thus.
notes: The long absolute clause is read as: sun (loc.) ... moon (loc.) ... world (loc.) ..., then the main clause. "tasmin" refers to visarga of unit 19. "māhendra-salila" = water of Mahendra (Indra): literal. "yathākramam" is placed with the tastes and the strength.
lines_deva: तस्मिन्नपि कालमार्गमेघवातवर्षाभिहतप्रभावे दक्षिणायनगेऽर्के शशिनि चाव्याहतबले शिशिराभिर्भाभिः शश्वदाप्यायमानेमाहेंद्रसलिलप्रशांतसंतापे जगत्यरूक्षा रसाःप्रवर्द्धंतेऽम्ललवणमधुरा यथाक्रमं बलं चोपचीयते नृणामिति ॥
lines_iast: tasminnapi kālamārgameghavātavarṣābhihataprabhāve dakṣiṇāyanage'rke śaśini cāvyāhatabale śiśirābhirbhābhiḥ śaśvadāpyāyamānemāheṃdrasalilapraśāṃtasaṃtāpe jagatyarūkṣā rasāḥpravarddhaṃte'mlalavaṇamadhurā yathākramaṃ balaṃ copacīyate nṛṇāmiti ||

hindi: और इस विषय में यह है।
english: And on this matter there is the following.
notes: Conventional introduction to a verse (units 22 onward).

hindi: हेमंत और शिशिर में विसर्ग और आदान का बल सर्वोत्तम होता है; शरद और वसंत में मध्यम; और वर्षा और ग्रीष्म में हीन।
english: In Hemanta and Śiśira the strength of visarga and ādāna is the best; in Śarad and Vasanta it is middling; in Varṣā and Nidāgha (the hot season) it is low.

text_flags.why: possible: the line is a graded series best / middling / low (agrya, madhya, hīna); "āpya" (watery) breaks the series, and āpya and agrya are close in Devanagari; metre is 8 syllables either way

notes: The editors flag the Hindi/English layers as loose. Printed "cāpyaṃ" would be "and watery"; I read cāgryaṃ "and best" on grounds of sense (possible, not certain). "visarga-ādānayoḥ balam": the strength belonging to the visarga and ādāna periods, i.e. at the end of visarga (Hemanta) and the start of ādāna (Śiśira), and so on; the text itself only gives the pairs of seasons. Nidāgha is the hot season (Grīṣma). The verb is absent; "balam" is understood in the second line.

uncertain.note: [hindi/eng] Strength at end of visarga/start of adana is best; translation loose but acceptable — suggested: -

words.gloss: from the coldness of the wind

hindi: दिशाएँ और सूर्य धुएँ के समान धूसर, धूल से मंद और पाले से धुँधले मंडलों वाले होते हैं; वायु की शीतलता के कारण उत्तर रोमांच उत्पन्न करने वाला होता है।
english: The directions and the suns are smoke-grey, dim with dust, their discs clouded with frost; and the north, because of the coldness of the wind, makes the hair stand on end.
notes: "dik-ādityāḥ" is read as a dvandva "directions and suns" (so the first line has these as subject); the plural "ādityāḥ" is odd and may stand for the sun and its discs/rays, the book Hindi has "दिशाएँ और सूर्य". "uttaraḥ" may be the north direction or the north wind; "north" is kept. The adjectives are masculine plural, agreeing with the masculine dvandva. Editors flagged the translation layers (not the Sanskrit).

uncertain.note: [hindi/eng] दिगादित्याः (directions and suns) not translated; sentence structure odd — suggested: add "दिशाएँ और सूर्य"

words.gloss: elephants, goats, buffaloes, horses, crows, pigs

hindi: रोध, प्रियंगु, पुन्नाग और लवली फूलों से दीप्त होते हैं; हाथी, बकरे, भैंसे, घोड़े, कौए और सूअर मदमस्त होते हैं।
english: Rodha, priyaṅgu, punnāga and lavalī (plant names) are bright with blossoms; elephants, goats, buffaloes, horses, crows and pigs are spirited.

text_flags.why: possible: the plant name is usually rodhra/lodhra; the book Hindi reads लोध्र; the metre (16) is fine either way

notes: Plant names kept as printed and not identified. The text does not say "forests"; the first line only names the plants. "dṛptāḥ" read as spirited/excited (proud); "sūkara" = pig/boar.

words.gloss: at the coming of the cold

hindi: हिम के आने पर नदियाँ, जो हिम की परतों से ढकी हैं और जिनमें मछलियाँ और पक्षी छिपे रहते हैं, भाप से युक्त और उष्ण होती हैं, और कुओं के जल भी।
english: At the coming of the cold (hima), the rivers, covered with sheets of snow, with fish and birds hidden away, are steaming and warm, and so are the waters of wells.
notes: The first-line adjectives are read with "nadyaḥ" (line 2); whether they also qualify the well waters is unclear. "līna" read as hidden/clinging. "himānī" = a mass of snow/frost. "hima-āgame" = at the coming of cold/snow (onset of the cold season).

hindi: शीत में ठंडी वायु से आहत होकर शरीर की ऊष्माएँ भीतर प्रवेश करती हैं, और पेट में उस अग्नि को, जिसकी ऊष्मा एकत्र हो गई है, प्रबल कर देती हैं।
english: In the cold, struck by the cold wind, the heats of the body enter inside, and in the belly they make the fire, its heat massed together, strong.

text_flags.why: extra anusvāra after "to": viśantaḥ + antaḥ gives viśanto'ntaḥ

notes: "piṇḍita-ūṣmāṇam" is read as an adjective of "analam" (its heat massed together). "śīte" read as locative "in the cold (season)". The fire is that of the belly (jaṭhare); no more is said in the text.

hindi: विसर्ग में बलवानों के लिए प्रायः स्वभाव से अत्यंत भारी (आहार) उपयुक्त होता है; उसके उचित प्रयोग के लिए बृंहण अन्न और पान प्रयुक्त करे।
english: In visarga, for the strong, what is very heavy is generally suitable by nature; for the right use of that, one should apply bṛṃhaṇa (nourishing) foods and drinks.

text_flags.why: possible: "ādiguru" gives no sense; the editors suggest svabhāvād atiguru (very heavy). Caution: that makes the line 17 syllables, not 16, so svabhāvād guru (heavy) is an alternative

notes: The subject of "kṣamam" (neuter) is not stated; it is taken as the fire (analam) of the previous unit, and "balinām" as its owners. The object (what the fire can bear) is not stated: only "heavy". "tasya yuktaye" = for the right fitting/use of that (fire); the book Hindi has "to satisfy", which is less literal. Editors flagged the reading of line 1.

hindi: ईंधन के बिना वह अग्नि अन्यथा शांत हो जाती है, अथवा अत्यधिक प्रबल हो जाने के कारण इस मनुष्य की धातुओं को भी पचा डालती है; और तब उन धातुओं के क्षय से वायु …
english: Otherwise, without fuel, it (the fire) would subside; or else, through its excessive intensity, it would digest even this person's dhātus; and then, from their depletion, the wind (marut) ...
notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. The sense-complete verse looks like L2 (4.35) of this unit + L1 (4.36) of unit 29; L1 (4.34) of this unit goes with the preceding line. Translation follows the printed unit. The subject 'it' (the fire, agni) comes from the preceding text, outside this chunk; 'marut' (wind) is the subject of 'kupyet' in the next unit. 'anyathā' can mean 'otherwise' or 'in another way'. The book's English/Hindi take 'atyudīrṇatayā' with 'sīdet'; this draft takes it with 'pacet' (athavā introduces the second alternative). Either is grammatically possible.

hindi: अग्नि का सहचर वह वायु कुपित हो जाता है, क्योंकि वह शीत है, और शीत में विशेष रूप से। इसलिए शीत ऋतु में स्निग्ध तथा मधुर, अम्ल और लवण रसों का सेवन करे।
english: (The wind,) the companion of fire, becomes disturbed, being cold, and especially so in cold weather. Therefore, in the cold season one should use unctuous tastes: the sweet, sour and salty.

'tejaḥsahacaraḥ' is taken as the wind (marut of the previous unit), not as the fire itself. 'hime' is rendered 'in the cold season'; 'hima' is literally 'cold/snow'.

english: (Having) the cold wind warded off through contact with the limbs of plump women; in Śiśira the cold is greater, born of cloud, wind and rain.

hindi: और आदान से उत्पन्न रूखापन (भी) है; इसलिए पहले वाली विधि अधिक मात्रा में करनी चाहिए। वसंत में वायु दक्षिण की होती है और सूर्य की किरणें कुछ ताँबे जैसे रंग की होती हैं।
english: And dryness arises from ādāna ('taking'); therefore the former regimen should be carried out to a greater degree. Spring (vasanta) has the southern wind, and the sun has coppery-red rays.

'vasantaḥ' is nominative, so the verse is a nominal description of spring.

words.gloss: sharp emesis, smoke, gargling, nasal instillation

hindi: तब वह अग्नि को बाधित करता हुआ बहुत-से रोग उत्पन्न करता है। इसलिए इस (ऋतु) में तीक्ष्ण वमन, धूम, गंडूष और नावन का प्रयोग करे।
english: Then, hindering the fire (agni), it produces many diseases. Therefore, in this (season), sharp emesis, smoke, gargling and nasal instillation (are to be used).
notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. words.gloss: exercise, rubbing, honey, barley, wheat, dry-land (animals)

hindi: व्यायाम, उद्वर्तन, शहद, जौ, गेहूँ और जांगल प्राणियों का, तथा मित्रों, उद्यानों और मनोहर युवतियों का सेवन करे।
english: One should resort to exercise, rubbing (udvartana), honey, barley, wheat and dry-land (jāṅgala) animals, and to friends, gardens and charming young women.
notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. hindi: स्नान किया हुआ, भली-भाँति सजा हुआ, माला धारण किए हुए, चंदन और अगरु से लिप्त; नाना प्रकार के पात्रों में रखे हुए और सहकार तथा उत्पल से अंकित …
english: Bathed, well adorned, wearing a garland, anointed with sandal and aguru; (drinks) set in various vessels and marked with sahakāra (mango) and utpala (lotus) ...

words.gloss: heavy, cold, day-sleep, unctuous, sour, sweet

hindi: भारी, शीत, दिन की नींद, तथा स्निग्ध, अम्ल और मधुर का त्याग करे। ग्रीष्म में अतसी के फूल जैसा, तीक्ष्ण किरणों वाला (सूर्य), दावानल से प्रदीप्त …
english: One should avoid the heavy and cold, daytime sleep, and the unctuous, sour and sweet. In summer, (the sun,) resembling the atasī flower, sharp-rayed, kindled by forest fire ...

hindi: दिशाएँ जलती हैं और भूमि भी; वायु किसी भी ओर से सुखद नहीं है। वायु, धूप और पसीने से प्राणी मानो ज्वर से पीड़ित हो जाते हैं।

hindi: ताल के पंखों की हवाएँ, हार, कमल और उत्पल सहित मालाएँ; तथा कमलनाल के कंगनों वाली, कृशांगी, चंदन से लिप्त प्रियतमाएँ।
english: Breezes from palm-leaf fans, necklaces, garlands with lotuses and water-lilies; and slender beloved women with bracelets of lotus-stalks, smeared with sandal.

text_flags.why: sraj (garland) has no t; acc. pl. srajaḥ

notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. The sense-complete verse looks like L2 (4.79) of this unit + L1 (4.80) of unit 51; L1 (4.78) of this unit goes with the preceding line. Translation follows the printed unit. 'tanvī' may describe the women (slender) or the bracelets; read as the women. The governing verb is 'niṣeveta' in the next unit. 'tālavṛnta' = palm-leaf fan (literally 'palm stalk').

hindi: सरोवरों, बावड़ियों, नदियों और वनों का, जो शीतल और सुगंधित हों, तथा अत्यंत हल्के वस्त्रों का सेवन करे।
english: One should resort to lakes, tanks, rivers and groves, cold and fragrant ones, and to very light garments.
notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. The sense-complete verse looks like L2 (4.81) of this unit + L1 (4.82) of unit 52; L1 (4.80) of this unit goes with the preceding line. Translation follows the printed unit. 'surabhīṇi' could qualify the water-places, or the garments, or both; 'vāpī' = tank/pond (often stepped).

lines_iast: sarāṃsi vāpīḥ saritaḥ kānanāni himāni ca ||

words.gloss: in which water falls from a contrivance

hindi: दिन में, जहाँ यंत्र से जल गिर रहा हो ऐसे धारागृह में सोए; और रात में सुगंधित फूलों से बिछे खुले आकाशतल पर।
english: By day one should sleep in a shower-house (dhārāgṛha) where water falls from a contrivance; and at night on an open-air roof (ākāśa-talaka) strewn with fragrant flowers.
notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. The sense-complete verse looks like L2 (4.83) of this unit + L1 (4.84) of unit 53; L1 (4.82) of this unit goes with the preceding line. Translation follows the printed unit. 'yantra' is any device or machine; 'water falling from a contrivance' avoids saying fountain. 'ākāśatalaka' is literally 'sky-surface', taken as an open roof or terrace.

words.gloss: with limbs moistened with camphor and sandal

hindi: कपूर और चंदन से भीगे अंगों वाला और जिसका कामसंग विरल हो; वर्षा ऋतु में वायु वारुण होती है और सब धान्यों का उगना होता है।
english: With limbs moistened with camphor and sandal, and with rare union with Anaṅga (love); in the rains the wind is Vāruṇa, and all crops spring up.
notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. The sense-complete verse looks like L2 (4.85) of this unit + L1 (4.86) of unit 54; L1 (4.84) of this unit goes with the preceding line. Translation follows the printed unit. 'anaṅga' is the god of love, so 'anaṅgasaṅgama' = sexual union. 'vāruṇaḥ' = of Varuṇa, i.e. western (or watery); 'varṣāsu' is plural locative (the rainy months).

words.gloss: dimmed gently by clouds blue like cut sapphire

words.gram: f. nom. pl. (dīrghikāḥ, visarga dropped before voiced n)

words.gloss: new water floods; rows of sky-stairs

hindi: भिन्न इंद्रनील जैसे नीले बादलों से धीरे-धीरे धुँधला हुआ आकाश; लंबी वापिकाएँ, नए जल की बाढ़, आकाश की सीढ़ियों की पंक्तियाँ …
english: The sky, gently dimmed by clouds blue like cut sapphire; the long tanks (dīrghikā), (with) floods of new water, (and) rows of sky-stairs ...

text_flags.why: possible: corrupt or mis-split compound; 'nabhaḥ' (sky) in 'nabhaḥ-sopāna' is unexplained

notes: GROUPING: the printed units pair the second half of one verse with the first half of the next. L2 (4.87) of this unit goes with the following line (next chunk); L1 (4.86) goes with the preceding line. Translation follows the printed unit. Second line is unclear: 'dīrghikā' is singular, 'paṅktayaḥ' plural, and the relation of 'nabhaḥ-sopāna' (sky-stairs) to the rest is uncertain; perhaps the tanks' rows of steps are compared to a stairway to the sky, or the compound is one phrase 'dīrghikā-nava-vāri-ogha-nabhaḥ-sopāna-paṅktayaḥ'. 'mandamanda' is read as 'gently/slowly'. The sentence continues in the next chunk.

words.gloss: lotuses ruined by heavy blows of water-streams

hindi: जल की धाराओं के भारी आघात से हुई क्षति के कारण नष्ट हुए कमल होते हैं; नदियाँ समुद्र जैसे आकार की होती हैं, और पृथ्वी पर जल तथा स्थल का भेद अस्पष्ट हो जाता है।
english: The lotuses are ruined by the damage from the heavy blows of streams of water; the rivers are ocean-shaped; and the earth has water and land indistinct.

text_flags.why: asita (dark) would change the sense; reading uncertain, āśita kept

notes: Sentence is a nominal description of the rainy season; no verb. 'sāgarākārā' is sāgara-ākārāḥ (visarga lost by sandhi before bh-). 'āśita' is taken as 'consumed, ruined' (the book reads 'damaged'); reading uncertain. Subject of the second line is bhūḥ (earth), also the implied subject of units 56-57.

words.gloss: resounding with deep thunder of clouds, peacocks, frogs
lit by indragopa insects, bow-fragments, lightning flashes

hindi: पृथ्वी बादलों की गहरी गर्जना तथा मोरों और मेंढकों की आवाज़ से गूँजती है, और इंद्रगोप कीटों, धनुष के खंडों तथा बिजली की चमक से प्रकाशित होती है।
english: The earth resounds with the deep thunder of clouds and the cries of peacocks and frogs, and is lit up by indragopa insects, fragments of the bow, and flashes of lightning.
notes: Feminine singular participles continue bhūḥ of the previous unit. 'dhanuḥ-khaṇḍa' (pieces of a bow) is taken as pieces of the rainbow (Indra's bow); the Sanskrit says only 'bow'. 'indragopa' is an insect name, kept as is.

words.gloss: weak because of the ādāna period

hindi: चारों ओर गहरी हरी घास वाली तथा शिलींध्र और कुटज से उज्ज्वल पृथ्वी है। उस समय, जब आदान के कारण शरीर निर्बल हो, अग्नि मंद हो और फिर से बाधित हो,
english: All around, with dark-green grass and bright with śilīndhra and kuṭaja, is the earth. At that time, when the body is weak because of the ādāna period, and the fire (agni) is dull and afflicted again,
notes: Second sentence continues into the next unit (locative absolute: body weak, agni dull and afflicted again by the doṣas named in 58; main verb niṣeveta in 58). 'ādānābale' is taken as ādāna-abale 'weak because of ādāna' (the 'taking-away' part of the year); 'ādāna' is not explained in this unit. śilīndhra, kuṭaja: plant names, not identified.

words.gloss: spoiled by rain, ground-vapour, sour change of water
one who has completed the course of cleansing

hindi: वर्षा, भूमि की भाप और जल के अम्ल पाक से दूषित हुए चल अर्थात वात आदि के द्वारा बाधित होने पर, शोधन का क्रम पूरा कर लेने के बाद बस्ति कर्म का सेवन करना चाहिए।
english: —afflicted by the cala (Vāta) and the others, which are spoiled by rain, vapour from the ground, and the sour transformation of water—one should resort to the basti procedure, having completed the course of cleansing (saṃśodhana).
notes: Completes the clause begun in 57 (agni afflicted by cala etc.). 'cala' (the mobile one) is taken as Vāta; 'ādi' = the other doṣas. 'amla-pāka' is the sour transformation (pāka) of water, kept literal.

words.gram: karmadhāraya, m. acc. sg. (collective; or purāṇa-śālīn with -n lost)

hindi: पुराना शालि चावल, गेहूँ और जौ तैयार किए हुए यूष और रसों के साथ लेना चाहिए; हानिरहित मदिरा, अरिष्ट और मार्द्वीक, अथवा बहुत थोड़ा जल।
english: One should take old śāli rice, wheat and barley with prepared yūṣas and broths (rasa); harmless madirā, ariṣṭa and mārdvīka, or else a very small amount of water.
notes: No verb in the unit: niṣeveta (58) or bhajet (61) is understood. 'nirgadam' (free of disease, harmless) could qualify the drinks or be adverbial; taken with the drinks. 'purāṇaśāli' ends in -i (singular form of a collective, or lost -n of purāṇaśālīn). yūṣa = a thin pulse soup, rasa = broth: kept as Sanskrit.

hindi: दिव्य जल, उबाला हुआ कुएँ का जल, चौण्ड्य जल अथवा सरोवर का ही जल; और वर्षा तथा वायु से व्याकुल दिन में भोजन ऐसा हो जो क्लेद और वात को जीतने वाला हो।
english: Rainwater (divya), well-water that has been boiled, cauṇḍya water, or lake water; and on a day troubled by rain and wind, the food should be such as overcomes dampness (kleda) and Vāta.
notes: 'cauṇḍya' is obscure: perhaps water of a cuṇḍa/cuṇḍī (small pool or tank); the book says pond water. 'divya' (heavenly) is water from the sky, i.e. rain. The verb is not stated (drinking, then 'is to be' for food). 'sārasam eva vā' is odd (eva before vā) but kept as printed.

words.gloss: at the rising of dense clouds

hindi: अच्छी तरह सूखा, हल्का, स्निग्ध, गरम, खट्टा और नमकीन भोजन करना चाहिए; और घने बादल उठने पर अधिकतर अन्न-पान शहद सहित तथा संस्रुत अर्थात छाना हुआ हो।
english: One should take food that is well dried, light, unctuous, hot, sour and salty; and when dense clouds rise, food and drink, mostly with honey and saṃsruta (strained; sense uncertain).
notes: 'saṃsruta' is uncertain: the book glosses it 'thick'; the participle of saṃ-√sru means flowed together or drained/strained, and 'strained' is used here. 'prāyaḥ' could also go with the first half. 'ghanodaya' could mean the rising of clouds or the time when clouds are dense.

uncertain.note: [hindi/eng] "संस्रुतं" glossed "thick/गाढ़े"; संस्रुत more likely strained/filtered — suggested: संस्रुतम् = strained (clear)

words.gloss: free from crawling creatures, ground-vapour, cold wind, spray

hindi: ऐसा घर जो रेंगने वाले जीवों, भूमि की भाप, ठंडी हवा और फुहारों से रहित हो; आग ले जाने के साधन से युक्त हो; और डाँस, मच्छर तथा चूहों से रहित हो।
english: A dwelling that is free from crawling creatures, ground-vapour, cold wind and spray; that has a fire-carrier (portable fire); and that is free from biting flies, mosquitoes and rats.

text_flags.why: possible: daṃśa (gadfly, biting fly) needs anusvāra; 'nirdaśa' would give no sense here

notes: No verb is given (the verb for 'dwell' is not in the unit). The reading of the first compound is uncertain: whether a- negates only sarīsṛpa or the whole list; taken as the whole list. 'sāgniyāna' is obscure: sa-agni-yāna 'with a fire-carrier' (brazier) is taken; the book's Hindi reads 'with fire and vehicles'. The ending '-m' of 'nirdaṃśa-maśaka-undura-m' is the neuter agreeing with bhavanam.

uncertain.note: [hindi] "अग्नियान" glossed "अँगीठी और वाहनों" (same word as 1.4._43_ सांगारयान) — suggested: अग्नियान = portable fire-pot/brazier only

words.gloss: fond of rubbing, ointment-rubbing, bathing, smoke, agaru scent

hindi: रगड़ने, उबटन, स्नान, धूम और अगरु की गंध का प्रेमी हो; और श्रेष्ठ हथिनियों के साथ रंग-बिरंगे वस्त्रों से सजा हुआ चले।
english: Fond of rubbing, ointment-rubbing (udvartana), bathing, smoke, and the scent of agaru, one should go out with the foremost she-elephants, adorned with colourful clothes.
notes: 'dhūma-gandha-aguru' could also be 'the fragrant smoke of agaru'; kept as a list. 'yāyāt kareṇu-mukhyābhiḥ' is literally 'go with the chief she-elephants'; riding is not stated. agaru: drug/wood name.

words.gloss: frost, going on foot, exercise, sun-rays

hindi: नदी का जल, उदमन्थ, दिन की नींद, अत्यधिक द्रव और मैथुन, तथा पाला, पैदल चलना, व्यायाम और सूर्य की किरणों को छोड़ देना चाहिए।
english: One should avoid river water, udamantha (a drink of mantha mixed with water), day-sleep, excess of liquid and sexual intercourse, as well as frost, going on foot, exercise and the sun's rays.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed line has 15 syllables and a stray visarga; ahaḥ-svapna (day-sleep) restores 16 syllables and agrees with the book's 'sleeping by day'

notes: The first line is read as a dvandva (nadī-jala, udamantha, ahaḥ-svapna, ati-drava, maithuna) with an assumed missing 'ha'. Without the correction 'manthāḥ svapna' has no clear construction. 'tuṣāra' is taken as frost or mist; 'pāda-caraṇa' as walking on foot (the book's 'feet wet in dew' is not in the words). Both halves are objects of 'tyajet'.

words.gloss: with conspicuous kāśa, saptāhva and kumuda

hindi: शरद ऋतु में आकाश श्वेत बादलों वाला होता है और पृथ्वी थोड़े कीचड़ से चिह्नित होती है; वह प्रकट काश, सप्ताह्व और कुमुद वाली तथा शालि धान से भरपूर होती है।
english: In autumn the sky has white clouds, and the earth is marked with a little mud; the earth is rich in conspicuous kāśa, saptāhva and kumuda, and abounding in śāli rice.
notes: 'prakāśa' is taken as 'conspicuous, bright' qualifying the three plants; it could also be a separate first member. kāśa, saptāhva: plant names, not identified; kumuda is kept as the name.

words.gloss: from the departure of masses of clouds
crowded with lines of krauñca birds

hindi: बादलों के समूह के हट जाने से सूर्य तीखी किरणें बिखेरता है और भूरे रंग का होता है; दिशाएँ अत्यंत निर्मल और क्रौंच पक्षियों की पंक्तियों से भरी होती हैं।
english: With the departure of the masses of clouds, the sun scatters sharp rays and is tawny-coloured; the directions are very clear, crowded with lines of krauñca birds.

text_flags.why: possible: babhruvarṇo is singular against plural ativimalāḥ/diśaḥ; the reading babhruvarṇā ativimalāḥ (the directions tawny and very clear) would agree with diśaḥ; the printed text is kept

notes: 'babhruvarṇo' is read as babhru-varṇaḥ qualifying raviḥ (the sun), so the printed text needs no change; the book's editors suggest babhruvarṇā (qualifying diśaḥ), which would be a different reading. 'ākulā diśaḥ' is ākulāḥ diśaḥ (visarga dropped before d-). krauñca: a bird name, kept.

uncertain.note: [src/split] "बभ्रुवर्णोऽतिविमलाः" singular vs plural दिशः — suggested: बभ्रुवर्णा अतिविमलाः

words.gloss: by the jostling of fish hidden among lotuses and flocks of swans

hindi: कमलों के बीच छिपी मछलियों और हंसों के झुंडों की टकराहट से सरोवर लहरों के टूटने से ऊँचे उठे हुए और निर्मल होते हैं।
english: By the jostling of fish hidden among the lotuses and flocks of swans, the lakes are high with breaking waves, and clear.

text_flags.why: probable: 'salhīna' is not a word; saṃlīna or sallīna (hidden, clinging) fits, with l-h mis-scanned

notes: 'saṃlīna' may qualify only the fish ('fish hidden among the lotuses') or both fish and swans; taken with the fish. 'taraṅga-bhaṅga-tuṅga' could also be 'raised high by the breaking of waves'.

words.gloss: of those whose bodies are used to the cold of the rains

hindi: वर्षा की शीतलता के अभ्यस्त शरीर वाले लोग जब सहसा ही सूर्य की किरणों से तप जाते हैं, तब पहले से संचित पित्त कुपित हो जाता है।
english: In those whose bodies are used to the cold of the rainy season, when they are suddenly heated by the sun's rays, the Pitta that was accumulated earlier then becomes aggravated.
lines_deva: तप्तानां संचितं पूर्वं तदा पित्तं प्रकुप्यति ॥
lines_iast: taptānāṃ saṃcitaṃ pūrvaṃ tadā pittaṃ prakupyati ||

hindi: सदा प्रशस्त हैं: तिक्त द्रव्यों के साथ घृत का पान, विरेचन और रक्त निकालना; और शीतल तथा हल्का अन्न-पान, एवं कषाय, मधुर और तिक्त पदार्थ।
english: Always recommended are drinking ghee with bitter things, purgation, and the flow of blood (bloodletting); also cold, light food and drink, and what is astringent, sweet and bitter.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tiktai-haviḥ' lacks the r of the instrumental plural before h; the editors also suggest tiktakahaviḥ

notes: 'sadā' could belong to the second half instead. 'asra-śruti' is literally 'flow of blood'. The last compound has no clear head noun: 'what is astringent, sweet and bitter' (taste, or substances) is taken. Whether 'tiktaiḥ haviḥ' means ghee prepared with bitters is an inference.

uncertain.note: [src] "तिक्तैहविः" malformed; Hindi says ghee processed with bitters — suggested: तिक्तकहविः or तिक्तैर्हविः

hindi: शालि और षष्टिक चावल, गेहूँ, जौ, मूँग, शर्करा और मधु; पटोल, आमलक, द्राक्षा, और अत्यंत भूखे लोगों के लिए जांगल पशुओं का मांस।
english: Śāli and ṣaṣṭika rice, wheat, barley, mudga, sugar and honey; paṭola, āmalaka, grapes, and the flesh of dry-land animals for those who are very hungry.
notes: Nominal list; 'śastam' of the previous unit is understood. 'bhṛśam' is taken with kṣudvatām ('very hungry'); it could modify the list. 'jāṅgala' is used as a noun (flesh of dry-land animals); paṭola and āmalaka are kept as drug names.

hindi: दिन में सूर्य की किरणों से तपा हुआ और रात में चंद्रमा की किरणों से शीतल किया हुआ, अगस्त्य द्वारा विषरहित किया गया जल,
english: Water heated by the sun's rays by day and made cool by the moon's rays at night, and made free of poison by Agastya,

text_flags.why: word division: the r belongs to the end of the previous token (karair)
probable: 'lhā' is a transposition for hlā (hlādita, made cool or glad)
possible: the instrumental of agastya is agastyena; 'agastena' is not a regular form

notes: The sentence continues into the next unit (the water is clear, pure, matured by time). 'Agastya' is left as the name; the text does not say more here (it is the star or sage of that name in tradition). Tokens 'divākarakarai' and 'rniśākarakarairniśi' have a misplaced space.

words.gloss: flocks of swans, flapping of wings

hindi: निर्मल, शुद्ध, समय से परिपक्व, पीने में अमृत के समान; और जहाँ हंसों के झुंडों के पंख फड़फड़ाने से भौंरों की पंक्तियाँ मँडराती हैं,
english: Clear, pure, matured by time, like nectar to drink; in places where rows of bees hover because of the flapping of the wings of flocks of swans,

text_flags.why: probable: bhramat + bhramara gives bhramadbhramara; 'ddhra' is a misprint

notes: The second line is one locative compound (haṃsa-ogha-pakṣa-vikṣepa-bhramat-bhramara-paṅktiṣu) printed with a space; it describes the lakes of the next unit (sarasīṣu), so the sentence continues. Taken as 'rows of bees hover (because of) the flapping of swans' wings'.

words.gloss: with light, clean clothes and a garland

hindi: और अच्छे कमलों से युक्त, सेवन के योग्य सरोवरों में तैरे; वह हल्के शुद्ध वस्त्र और माला धारण करे तथा शीतल उशीर का लेप लगाए।
english: And one should swim in lakes that are good to resort to, with fine lotuses; wearing light, clean clothes and a garland, and anointed with cool uśīra.

hindi: दो ऋतुओं के अंतिम और आरंभिक सात-सात दिन ऋतुसंधि कहे गए हैं। वहाँ पूर्व ऋतु की विधि छोड़नी चाहिए और बाद वाली क्रमशः अपनानी चाहिए।
english: The last seven days of one season and the first seven days of the next are called the ṛtusaṃdhi (junction of seasons). There the former regimen is to be given up and the latter taken up, step by step.
notes: 'antya-ādi-saptāhāt' is read as 'the last seven days (of the first season) and the first seven days (of the next)'; the ablative is loose. 'kramāt' is taken with both verbs: gradually, in order.

hindi: क्योंकि अचानक छोड़ने और अपनाने से असात्म्य से उत्पन्न रोग हो सकते हैं। इस प्रकार की ऋतुओं में ही देहधारियों के स्वास्थ्य के लिए भी विधि है।
english: For diseases born of unsuitability (asātmya) may arise from abrupt abandoning and taking up. In seasons of such a kind, this is the regimen for the health of embodied beings.
notes: 'asātmya' is kept as 'unsuitability'. 'ṛtuṣu evaṃvidheṣu eva' (in just such seasons) refers to normal seasons, contrasted with 'anyarūpeṣu' in the next unit. 'tyāga-śīlana' is read 'abandoning and practising (taking up)'.
